description: A1 English — first introductions, basic greetings, simple present

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Hi Carlos! Nice to meet you. How are you today?

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Hi. I am Carlos. I am... bien. Sorry, fine.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Nice. Remember: 'I AM from Mexico'. Try again.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: I am... ingeniero. Engineer? I am engineer.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Almost! 'I am AN engineer'. We use 'a' or 'an' before jobs.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Yes. I like... fútbol. Football. And I like cook.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: I like cookING. Add -ing for activities.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: I like cooking. And I like running.

summary.headline: First class — introductions, simple present 'to be', articles a/an, gerunds for hobbies.

keyMoments.description: Student applied -ing to a new verb without prompting

errorsDetected.explanation: El verbo 'to be' es obligatorio en presente simple en inglés.
Profesiones contables siempre llevan artículo a/an en inglés.
Después de 'like' para hobbies se usa gerundio (-ing).

homework.title: Write 10 sentences about yourself
homework.description: Use 'I am', 'I am from', 'I am a/an [job]', 'I like [activity-ing]'.

homework.title: Practice introductions with Lingo
homework.description: Have a 5-minute conversation introducing yourself. Use the structures from class.

nextClassRecommendations: Drill 'to be' affirmative + negative forms — still inconsistent
Introduce articles a/an with more profession examples
Add basic question forms (Where are you from? What do you do?)
expected.tutorPrivateNotes: Carlos parece motivado, mezcla bastante español pero entiende correcciones rápido. Es ingeniero en Guadalajara — usar contexto profesional en próximas clases (vocabulario técnico básico).
expected.sharedNotes: Welcome! In your first class you learned how to introduce yourself. Great job correcting yourself when I pointed things out. Keep practicing 'I am' before nouns and -ing for activities you like.
